statements.text: Over a file's read points. Finding 1 — no spread: no two points differ on a scored term by the term's floor or more; the floor is the value below which a difference between two configurations is not read (metrics doc §10). Finding 3 — spread the prior table missed: the row's quantity is at most (1 − g) of the quantity of the best point, g = 0.5, and the best point is better than the row on a scored term by the floor or more. The row is the configuration the oracle applies; the best point is the read point with the highest quantity. Read on the table, the row captures at most half of the improvement the best point reaches over fixed. Finding 2 — spread the prior table's row holds: neither of the two.

The route rule is fixed after the RQ0 run's data were seen. On the runs on disk the four files of decision 2's first kind are at finding 3 before any search run — the boot default is a point of the grid and their row is worse than it by the floor or more — so the route is known before the search: the table is rewritten. On c7-gaming the row reaches a frame miss rate of 0 against fixed's 1, so no point can beat it; on c7-transcode the row's quantity is 0.865; on c1-transcode the row's quantity is 0.005, and 62 of the file's 100 random runs exceed it by more than 0.01, the best at 0.153. The search runs as the statement failure-procedure requires, and its per-file findings are what Phase 12 is designed from.

The search runs at the primary alone: the blessed files, fixed at the primary boot default. Each of the gate's ten alternative boot defaults is a point of the grid, so each file's finding is recomputed with that point in place of fixed; a finding that changes is reported as a range over the boot default. No variant file was searched.
The search is read-only: nothing it finds is written into a table (_dev/docs/rq0-preparation-notes.md §4.3: ignore labels, sweep the configuration space, observe the spread).
